join_order.notes: Linear scan of info_type/info.off+.dat to resolve it_genres and it_rating ids
~12% of 2,528,312 titles; produce vector<int32_t> of movie ids T

join_order.build: movie_info[range mv] semi (it1==it_genres AND info IN {Horror,Thriller} AND note IS NULL)
join_order.notes: Walk movie_info__movie_id__offsets[mv..mv+1); short ranges (~6 rows). Use flat_hash_set<string_view>{Horror,Thriller} for mi.info; note IS NULL via note.off[i]==note.off[i+1]
Walk movie_info_idx__movie_id__offsets[mv..mv+1); compare info row slice lexicographically against '8.0' (memcmp + length tiebreak)

join_order.build: cast_info[range mv] (note IN writer-set AND n_gender[person_id-1]==g_f)
join_order.notes: Walk cast_info__movie_id__offsets[mv..mv+1); for each ci row, check note via flat_hash_set<string_view> of 5 writer roles, then direct array lookup n_gender[person_id-1]==g_f

filters.predicate: info_type_id = it_genres AND info IN ('Horror','Thriller') AND note IS NULL

data_structures.name_gender_array: raw int8_t array (mmap of name/gender.bin), direct index by person_id-1
data_structures.title_driver: std::vector<int32_t> of movie ids (sorted ascending by id)
data_structures.min_aggregates: three std::string holding current MIN(mi.info), MIN(mi_idx.info), MIN(t.title); guarded with a per-thread local then merged
data_structures.indexes_mmap: offsets_only int32_t arrays for cast_info/movie_info/movie_info_idx by movie_id

parallelism.notes: Partition title id range [1..2528312] into morsels (~64K each). Each thread filters production_year, then per surviving movie does the three offset-range probes. Per-thread MIN buffers merged at end.
